It has no integrator-addressed section and must not: it IS the integrator's record, and a close that addressed items to itself would be the reconciliation defect in miniature. Its own findings go to wave 37 as registered residuals and deferred decisions, which is the mechanism that exists for them.

hand_sweep.note: What the sweep cannot reach, swept by hand and recorded so the close's coverage is not confused with the tool's.
items: The 26 seam commits --uncarded returned were classified by eye, one by one: 22 are cards' OWN code commits (write-lend-tasks-exercise 5, mutex-share-cross-emission 6, joined-provenance-call-frames 4, w36-corpus-contracts-3 3, card-scope-guard 2, stability-reeval-2 1, c-gateway-indirect-census-2 1), 3 are integrator corrections (b5cfc2cb, e4619e37, 2200a04e) and 1 is the wave-open commit 60958bf0. Total 22+3+1=26. ZERO are uncarded work: every commit is attributable to a card, to the integrator, or to the wave's opening.

The 44 residual-shaped names were classified individually, not in bulk: 18 registered, 15 card names rather than residuals, 8 discharged with the discharging card named, 2 rules or prospective names rather than open work, 1 a deferred decision. 18+15+8+2+1=44.

--residuals fell 44 -> 25 after registration. NINETEEN names went quiet, not eighteen: C-GATEWAY-INDIRECT-CENSUS-2 also dropped, because a registered entry's `source` path contains that card's own name and the scan is case-insensitive. The classification (a card name, not a residual) is right, but it went quiet for the WRONG REASON, and a future close should not read that drop as a decision anyone took.

AGENTS.md's headline numbers were re-read from their sources rather than from the ledger: named_followups against the matrix file itself, the CT row against docs/reevaluation/ct_manifest.json's own stage data through the card reports, the contract corpus against compiler/tests/qcore_contract_corpus.rs's pinned tables, and the merged-gate row against this close's own measured logs.

main MOVED DURING THIS CLOSE. At the close's start `main` was fa48211a, the brief's base; it is now 477b733d, 'Open wave 37: create the increment record and move the index pointer before any card launches'. That commit is the integrator's wave-37 opening, not wave-36 work, and its own message says 'Wave 36's close paragraph still belongs in wave-36.md', which agrees with this close's brief. The consequence to know at merge time: the increment index will already name wave-37.md, so a literal reading of the sync rule would misfile this close's paragraph. It is in wave-36.md.

Constraint 16's list is now recorded as KNOWN INCOMPLETE rather than assumed complete: LOAD-SENSITIVE-ROW-UNNAMED names a seventh test showing the same signature in the same crate, measured by a different card than the one that measured the sixth row.

deferred_decisions.note: Fifteen decision ENTRIES were carried into this close across two files - seven in docs/reports/wave34-close/deferred_decisions.json and eight in docs/reports/wave35-close/reconciliation.json - over eight distinct names, of which SIX were still open. Restated here, not resolved, except where a wave-36 card resolved one and is named. Two new decisions are raised by this wave's cards. The two already ended at wave 35 are recorded so the 15-entry carry is accounted rather than silently reduced to 6.

items.name: CT10-REASON-ROW
items.ground: Still deferred, a fourth wave. NO new evidence from wave 36: no card touched the CT corpus's unmapped cases, and CT-CTWIN-LANE's wave-35 re-measurement (CT10 stays unmapped 'on half a scenario') remains the last word. NEW THIS WAVE, and it is about the mechanism rather than the decision: card STABILITY-REEVAL #2 also registered this name as a named_followup, so it is now carried by BOTH mechanisms - see DECISION-ALSO-REGISTERED-AS-FOLLOWUP, registered by this close. Resolving the decision will not retire the entry.

items.name: MATRIX-UPDATED-STALE-AT-WAVE-27
items.ground: Still deferred; the decision is untaken and this close does not take it. NEW EVIDENCE: the matrix was regenerated at every wave-36 merge that touched it and once more by this close with its own gate, so the `updated` field's wave-27 prose now sits beside a file regenerated nine waves later. The divergence widens with every close, which is an argument for taking the decision and not for taking it a particular way. Also now double-carried as a named_followup (DECISION-ALSO-REGISTERED-AS-FOLLOWUP).

items.name: EXAMPLES-STYLE-SLICE-FANOUT
items.ground: Still deferred, a fourth wave. No card of wave 36 touched examples/ and this close produces NO new evidence about it. Re-listed so it does not expire in silence, which is the whole point of the re-listing mechanism; a close that invented a disposition here would be making the record worse.

items.name: SYNC-RULE-TOOLING-COMMIT-SCOPE
items.ground: Still deferred, and wave 36 sharpens it again. --uncarded returned 26 commits, of which FOUR are exactly the shapes the decision is about: the wave-open commit 60958bf0, and THREE integrator corrections - b5cfc2cb (the stated follow-on count), e4619e37 and 2200a04e (re-separating three wave-35 increment entries a union merge had fused, then rebuilding it when the first attempt inserted nine blank lines instead of three). Two of the three change a committed document's content with no card report, which is the question. Wave 35 saw four such commits; wave 36 has four again, so this is a steady state rather than an anomaly, and steady states are what rules are for.

items.name: PLATFORM-RESIDUAL-FAMILY-PARTIALLY-TRACKED
items.ground: Still deferred, and this close deliberately did NOT resolve it by completing the registration, for the reason the wave-35 close gave: the decision is precisely WHICH arm to take - complete the registration, or state the rule that keeps platform residuals out of the matrix - and taking one silently would be the close deciding it. NEW EVIDENCE: wave 36 added another platform residual of exactly this family, WRITE-LEND-EXERCISE-WINDOWS-RUN, and that one IS registered - so the family is now more partially tracked than before, not less.

items.name: DOCS-COMPACT-CADENCE-DOES-CORRECTION-WORK
items.ground: Still deferred - explicitly a question raised for the user, which no card and no close may answer. NEW EVIDENCE from this close, offered as a data point and not as an argument for either reading: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md GREW again here, and every single addition was a correction landing late - three unapplied constraint amendments, constraint 14's missing wave-36 entry, and two hygiene rules a card asked for. None of it is narrative accretion, which is the reading the decision has to choose between. DOCS-COMPACT-7 is due around wave 37 and will inherit the question.

items.name: VERIFIER-HOST-ROW-DISPOSITION
items.ground: Ended at the WAVE-35 close, not here; recorded so the 15-entry carry is accounted rather than silently dropped. Wave 36 adds a measurement that supports the resolution rather than reopening it: the row passed 12/12 in isolation at load 23.7-27.6 and failed once in-gate at ~40, which is a load-sensitivity finding about a repaired mechanism and not the unresolved validation finding the decision was about.

items.name: items
items.ground: Not a decision. It was a reader artifact - a bogus name the wave-34 file's shape produced - withdrawn at the wave-35 close and recorded here only because it is one of the 15 carried entries and an unexplained disappearance is what this record exists to prevent.

items.name: INDIRECT-CENSUS-FEATURE-UNBUILT
items.ground: RAISED BY WAVE 36, card C-GATEWAY-INDIRECT-CENSUS-2 section 12.2, which states it is a decision and not a task and declines to take it. Both arms are written down: add a CI job building `-p qcore-c-gateway --features indirect-census`, or record that the instrumentation is disposable and a future census re-derives it. The answer depends on whether wave 37 takes a gateway card at all, and the card's own recommendation is that it should not take this one. Also registered as a named_followup so the work is tracked either way.

items.name: TASK-ROUTE-TSAN-SEGV-PRIORITY
items.ground: RAISED BY WAVE 36, card WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE section 11 item 7, which declines to set the priority and says the choice is the user's. The finding behind it is route-wide rather than card-local: the whole checked concurrency route has NO thread-sanitizer evidence, and no TSan row exists anywhere in this repository. The decision is whether that is wave-37 card work or a follow-on; the residual TASK-ROUTE-TSAN-SEGV is registered either way, so nothing is lost by carrying the decision.
